Rebec­ca Clar­ren was over­come when she learned that her family’s land in Jew Flats, South Dako­ta — the basis of their com­fort­able, mid­dle-class life in Amer­i­ca — was stolen from the Lakota.

The 1862 Home­stead Act promised 160 acres to those who built a home and tilled the land, whether they were cit­i­zens or not. What a gift this must have seemed like to the impov­er­ished Russ­ian Jews who were for­bid­den to own land in their own coun­try. Intrigued by posters about free land in the Dako­tas, 75 , 000 Russ­ian Jews — Clarren’s ances­tors among them — went West.
